messages.body_plain:
hi, I don't know RADmeth has a way to deal with batch effects. afaik you can include batches as covariates, but you can do the same in methylKit.

I just didn't have any dataset that had a strong unknown batch effect, the type that you can identify via SVA. If someone can send me a minimal data set that shows an unknown batch effect, I can have look into the SVA based solution.

Best,
Altuna

I remember I did it by exporting the data in numeric format in text file. Then I loaded it back into R and performed SVA on it and saved it so that I could load it into methylkit again. In the end it was pretty straight-forward, but now I couln'd find the code any longer. There was a change in the results. I did it because there was a batch effect in the same samples in RNA-seq. Later on I moved to another project. The analysis was redone by other people with MethylKit but this time no batch effect correction was made. I asked about it and the people who did it said that they thought the data didn't need it because the RRBS data usually has less batch effect.

Jussi

messages.subject_clean: normalizeCoverage() function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to know a bit better how the normalizeCoverage() function works.

I am analyzing a DNAme dataset using 500bp. I am allocation my samples into four groups so that I can understand the differences during the QC steps (correlation, clustering, PCA).

This is my procedure:

file.list = list(args[1],args[2],args[3],args[4],args[5],args[6],args[7],args[8],args[9],args[10])
sample.list=list(args[11],args[12],args[13],args[14],args[15],args[16],args[17],args[18],args[19],args[20])

methData=methRead(
  file.list,
  sample.id <http://sample.id>=sample.list,
  treatment=c(0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,3),
  assembly="hg19",
  header=TRUE,
  context="CpG",
  resolution="base",
  pipeline=list(
    fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,start.col=2,end.col=2,coverage.col=6,strand.col=3,freqC.col=5)
  )

tile500=tileMethylCounts(methData,win.size=500,step.size=100)
tile500.filtered=filterByCoverage(tile500,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
tile500.normalized=normalizeCoverage(tile500.filtered,method="median”)
tileMeth.normalized=unite(tile500.normalized,destrand=FALSE)

1) I am curios to understand how the normalization is done here. For instance, I specified four conditions in my treatment list (i.e., 0,1,2,3).

Is the normalization done between samples WITHIN each of the four groups or between samples irrespective of the group ID?

2) After normalization, I am reorganizing the tileMeth.normalized object so that I can calculate DMRs using a Fisher’s test on the pool conditions. For instance:

tileMeth2.normalized=reorganize(tileMeth.normalized,sample.ids=c(args[11],args[12],args[13],args[16],args[17],args[18],args[19],args[20]),treatment=c(1,1,1,0,0,0,0,0))
tileMeth2.pooled=pool(tileMeth2.normalized,sample.ids=c(“Treatment_1”,”Pooled_controls"),treatment=c(1,0))

Is the normalization I have performed before reorganizing and pooling affecting this step in any way?
Would I need to normalize again after I reorganize tileMeth.normalized, before pooling?

Thank you
Federico

>
> 1) I am curios to understand how the normalization is done here. For instance, I specified four conditions in my treatment list (i.e., 0,1,2,3).
>
> Is the normalization done between samples WITHIN each of the four groups or between samples irrespective of the group ID?
>

as far as I remember, it is done within samples doesn't care about groups.

>
> 2) After normalization, I am reorganizing the tileMeth.normalized object so that I can calculate DMRs using a Fisher’s test on the pool conditions. For instance:
>
> tileMeth2.normalized=reorganize(tileMeth.normalized,sample.ids=c(args[11],args[12],args[13],args[16],args[17],args[18],args[19],args[20]),treatment=c(1,1,1,0,0,0,0,0))
> tileMeth2.pooled=pool(tileMeth2.normalized,sample.ids=c(“Treatment_1”,”Pooled_controls"),treatment=c(1,0))
>
> Is the normalization I have performed before reorganizing and pooling affecting this step in any way?
> Would I need to normalize again after I reorganize tileMeth.normalized, before pooling?
>

I think it is OK if you have done the normalization once before pooling and reorganizing. You may need to redo it after pooling because I see that you have more samples in one group, once pooled one group will have systematically more coverage than the other.

for example: the ratio of unmethylated to methylated bases are the same in the following tests, but one has more coverage on one sample and it gets borderline significant values with higher coverage

fisher.test(t(matrix(c(10,20,15,15),ncol=2)))

fisher.test(t(matrix(c(10,20,150,150),ncol=2)))

also it might be worthwhile not to pool the data when you have replicates

Best,
Altuna
